# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

156	## Detailed Design
157	
158	### Core Rules
159	
160	Format: **Rule / Why / Edge notes**. Ids `SN-n` (the prefix is unused in any GDD or the registry; `HR-` is the art bible's id for its horror-rules and is not this system's). Units: one **run** is one `sanity.drift` invocation, `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` 12 ticks = 0.2 s (5 Hz), where `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` equals the kernel divisor 12 by relation (KRN:54, KRN:202) and is not a knob (the `SUIT_HP_FULL` precedent); 1 s = 5 runs; **the run clock is absolute: `run = T div 12`**, where `T` is the kernel tick the kernel persists and exposes in `kernel.clock`; the hook fires only when `T mod 12 = 0` (offset 0, divisor 12), so at a hook `run` is exact and monotonic across save, restore and an unbound stretch, and every stored run stamp (`start_run`, `active_run`, `end_run`, `debunked_run`, `until_run`, the debounce stamps, the `repaired_recent[]` stamps (reserved: none are written at the MVP, SN-17 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2)*), `batch_end_run`, `last_onset_run`) is an absolute `run` and never a per-seat count; `stage_dwell` and `harm_below_runs` are **executed-run counters** (an unbound seat freezes them but not the stamps, so a rebind sees every stamped window elapsed as if the seat had stayed bound) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING)*; `mSU` is the milli-sanity-unit, an integer that never reaches a player surface. Every Sanity-owned number is `[PLACEHOLDER]` and registered as such; every cited constant carries its registry value and owner. "Seat" means a PlayerId (1 in single-player).
161	
162	#### Block, hook and level

164	**SN-1. Three blocks, not one.**

166	
167	| block_id | class | scope | persist / persist_scope | repl_hint | restore_after | contents |
168	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
169	| `sanity.state` | SIM | PER_PLAYER (PlayerId) | true / **WORLD** | `SHARED_SUMMARY`; the projection is `{stage, tell_on, harm_eligible}` only | `[]` | `level` (mSU), `stage`, `stage_dwell`, `tell_on`, `harm_eligible`, `harm_below_runs`, `pending`, `last_tell_epoch`, `forced` (dev diagnostic, SN-28; outside the projection; always false in a release export) |
170	| `sanity.ledger` | SIM | PER_PLAYER | true / **WORLD** | `HOST_ONLY` | `[sanity.state, graph.state, layout.state]` and, *(Horror Entities, Designed; block `horror.state`, HE-3; status refreshed 2026-10-27 — design review)*, `horror.state` | `lies[]` {**lie_id**, slot, subject_ref `{stable_id, surface}`, kind, params, **direction**, state, onset_stage, start_run, active_run, end_run, debunked_run, leak_modes, first_lie}, `immune[]` {subject_ref, until_run}, per-subject lie visit counters (stream `"sanity.lie/<PlayerId>/<stable_id>"`, a map pruned at the first hook run after the subject's destruction, since Sanity has no destruction callback), RNG counters (`sanity.lure`, `sanity.phantom`, `sanity.hide`), **`evented[]`** (the subjects that have had their one lit-entry event in the current visit; replaces `lit_prev[]`), **`batch_end_run`**, `entry_pending`, `debounce[]`, `repaired_recent[]`, `horror_enc[]`, `lures[]`, `lies_seen` (counted on a lie's PENDING to ACTIVE step), the `incidents` ring, **`last_onset_run`** (absolute `run`, set on the accept run and read by the `LIE_GAP_S` gate; initial value on first bind `-1`, the one permitted negative, meaning "no onset yet" so the gap gate passes; any other stored value is `0` to `2^53`, and a value below `-1` is `COUNTER_RANGE`) and **`last_cid`** (the Graph compartment id the seat occupied at its last executed run, EXTERIOR id 0 for none; the visit detector compares it with the current `cid(P)`) and **`next_lie_id`** (the per-seat `lie_id` mint, starts 1, SN-23 entry schema) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `direction`, `evented[]` and `batch_end_run` added, `lit_prev[]` replaced, the `lies_seen` increment point moved, SN-15 L-D and SN-16)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING: `last_onset_run` and `last_cid` were read by the rules (SN-16 gap gate and visit definition) but held nowhere, so a restore reset the gap and the visit state; `last_onset_run` cannot be derived from `lies[]` because ended entries are removed. Both are in the SHAPE key set, AC-SN-2, 76, 98, 159 and the new AC-SN-173)* |
171	| `sanity.perception` | PERCEPTION_OUT | PER_PLAYER | **false** (derived) | `OWNER_PRIVATE` | none (rebuilt in `post_restore`) | the per-seat projection of the ledger (SN-23) |
172	
173	*Why.* CR-12 blinds Sanity's own hook to `PERCEPTION_OUT`, so active-lie state must be SIM; a block carries exactly one `repl_hint`, and the level's summary must reach every client (the victim must see the attacker's tell) while the ledger must never reach another client. Splitting by `repl_hint` turns "no reader but Sanity and DIAGNOSTIC" into a block-level lint instead of a field-level one. *(Orchestrator ruling R2, ADR candidate: ledger placement.)*
174	*Edge notes.* The ledger is a deliberate Pillar 4 oracle risk: a sim system that read it would learn which surface lies. The lint is "no symbol of `sanity.ledger` is read outside `sanity/` except by the Debug Overlay as DIAGNOSTIC" (an AC in Acceptance Criteria). `evented`, `batch_end_run`, `entry_pending` and `debounce` are state, not caches: if rebuilt in `post_restore` from the world at the snapshot tick, a snapshot taken between hook runs could rebuild a different set than the uninterrupted run held, and the kernel's `state_hash` (G4, CR-13) would diverge. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `lit_prev` became `evented`, SN-16.)* PlayerId keys are stable seat ids, never `peer_id` (KRN:52, 100). *Closed reason sets (QA-11).* `SANITY_BOOT_*` (registry: `SANITY_BOOT_REASONS`), one per assertion: `LEAD_INVARIANT` (D.4 (i) to (iv)), `AMBIENT_FLOOR_MISSING`, `AMBIENT_FLOOR_INVARIANT` (D.8 (a) to (c)), `HOME_REFUGE_INVARIANT` (D.8 (d)), `SUB_CAP_INVARIANT` (D.8 (e)), `HARM_HYSTERESIS` (D.9), `THRESHOLD_ORDER` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: the threshold-ordering assertion `0 < SAN_HARM_ENTER < SAN_HARM_EXIT` and `SAN_TELL_ON + STAGE_HYST <= SAN_TELL_OFF` and `STAGE_ENTER[3] + 2 x STAGE_HYST <= STAGE_ENTER[2]` and `STAGE_ENTER[2] + 2 x STAGE_HYST <= STAGE_ENTER[1] < SAN_MAX`, so a retune can never invert a threshold pair)*, `IMMUNITY_INVARIANT` (`DEBUNK_IMMUNE_S >= max(LIE_GAP_S)`), `FIELD_CHECK_FLOOR` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: lies above `DECOY_OVERLAYS_MAX`), `LIE_TARGET_DATA` (a `lie_targets.json` surface outside the module-body channel, a seam-lane valve or breaker entry (MSA F1), a lie kind with no leak, or *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING)* a comfort-capable surface whose `loop` has no L-G guard row), `HIDE_STANDOFF` (`HIDE_SAFE_R` at or below Horror's `LURK_STANDOFF_PX`, SN-22). `SANITY_RESTORE_*` (registry: `SANITY_RESTORE_REASONS`), one per failure class: `SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`, `SHAPE` (missing or extra key), `LEVEL_RANGE`, `STAGE_RANGE`, `COUNTER_RANGE`, `LIE_KIND_UNKNOWN`, `LIE_TIME_ORDER` (not `start_run <= active_run <= end_run`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, BLOCKING: `SUBJECT_UNRESOLVED` leaves the closed set. A well-formed `subject_ref` that no longer resolves after the Graph and Layout blocks restore is a legitimate dead ref, not corruption: a subject may be destroyed or salvaged between hook runs and the snapshot may be taken before the next run. It is handled by the next hook run (SN-23, EC-SN-30); only a malformed ref is `SHAPE`.)* A boot reason refuses boot; a restore reason fails that block's two-phase restore and leaves the pre-restore state unchanged. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: **JSON number typing.** A JSON-parsed integer arrives in GDScript as a `float`, so the SHAPE check accepts any integer-valued, finite float for an integer field and re-casts it to `int` before range checks and hashing; a fractional value, NaN or infinity fails `SHAPE`. AC-SN-76 carries the JSON round-trip and the two-insertion-order cases.)*
175	
176	**SN-2. One hook and a fixed run order.**
177	*Rule.* One hook: `(hook_id sanity.drift, owner sanity, divisor 12, offset 0, after: [{graph.propagate.failure, tolerates_stale: true}, attention.step, emitter.place, body.integrate, interaction.step, {suit.vitals, tolerates_stale: true}, horror.step])`. Sanity reads Suit's bands and cue-relevant state and Horror's `horror.view`; neither reads `sanity.state` in its hook (Suit never reads sanity, SN-19; Horror reads only the SIM view `sanity_view`, a committed projection of the previous run), so no cycle forms. Registry request on `sanity.drift`.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `interaction.step` is added. Interaction now calls `record_falsification` from `interaction.step` on the completion tick (IA-30), and that hook is `after: [controller.step, emitter.place]`, so without an edge the order of the two hooks on a shared tick would be a registration tie that CR-3 forbids relying on, and EC-SN-12, EC-SN-13 and AC-SN-66 and AC-SN-128 assume the falsification lands first. No cycle: nothing Interaction orders after reads Sanity's hook. Registry request on `sanity.drift`.)* Sanity registers no command, no `INPUT_SURFACE`, no PLAYER-origin anything in the MVP; its only writes are inside its own hook and its two Class B mutators. For each bound seat in ascending PlayerId, a run does, in this order: (1) snapshot inputs (Attention view, Graph reads, the seat's section and position, the lit set, `body_is_home`, `ring`); (2) D.1 drift: exposure, recovery, pending drain, level update; (3) D.2 stage, then the `tell_on` flag and D.3 harm gate; (4) ledger upkeep: PENDING to ACTIVE activations with witness re-check, EXPIRED, INVALIDATED, pruning of `immune[]`, and the INVALIDATE-and-prune of every ledger entry whose `subject_ref` no longer resolves (a subject destroyed or salvaged since the last run, or a dead ref carried through a restore, SN-23); (5) lit-entry events then D.5 onset (class b, and a, c, d if enabled); (6) rebuild `sanity.perception` in full from steps 3 to 5; (7) store the visit bookkeeping (`evented[]`, `batch_end_run`, `last_cid`) for the next run. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING: `last_cid` joins the stored bookkeeping; D.5 writes `last_onset_run` at step 5.)*
178	*Why.* Reads must see this tick's Attention phase, lit set and seat section at the coincidence `T mod 12 = 0`, and the Graph bands and Suit state as last committed (the stale-tolerant edges above); `graph.propagate.power` and Attention (divisor 6, offset 0) land on that tick, the Graph's `.atmo` and `.failure` and the Suit (offsets 2 and 4) do not *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so Sanity's work is O(seats x small constant). `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is a logging threshold shared with them, not a cap. Offset 0 versus 6 is the kernel owner's to rebalance if the coincident hooks breach it.
179	*Edge notes.* Conflict C6: the kernel's fixture label `sanity (12, 0)` (KRN:787) is an example, not this registration; the real id is `sanity.drift` and a wording check is routed to the kernel owner (reflexion P-10: examples are read as contracts). Hooks may submit SYSTEM commands; Sanity submits none. `horror.step` runs at divisor 5 (HE-4) and *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: is now in `after:`, so on the coinciding ticks it runs first)*; at a Sanity run `horror.view` is up to 4 ticks old since its last run, and up to **5** ticks counting the one-tick anchor lag of E8 (the bound earlier written as 4 undercounted the anchor lag; at most 5 x `V_HUNT_MPX`/1000 px of motion), which E3's 288 px radius and the HIDE collapse tolerate; Sanity never needs same-tick Horror state *(Horror Entities, Designed; status refreshed 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
180	
181	**SN-3. Level, units and seat lifecycle.**
182	*Rule.* `level` is an integer in `[0, SAN_MAX]` mSU, `SAN_MAX` 100000 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, set to `SAN_MAX` for a seat on its first bind in NEW_GAME. A seat first bound mid-game (VS-B join) starts at `SAN_MAX`; a PlayerId that already has stored state keeps it (no join-to-reset lever). Seat lifecycle (table in States and Transitions): an **unbound** seat does not drift, has no onset and retains its state under its PlayerId; a **DOWNED** seat drifts (exposure is real while down) and keeps onset; a **DEAD** seat freezes at the tick of death, and in the MVP death is the death stub (SL-7: reload the last autosave), so the frozen state is replaced by the restored one.
183	*Why.* Integer and JSON-safe (SL S-1), far below 2^53; the resolution (1 mSU per run) is below the slowest rate; the number never reaches a player (IA-39: "no sanity meter or number exists"). Death is not a cure (SL H3).
184	*Edge notes.* A guest joining a host world and whether a guest keeps a stage are Co-op's and Sanity Scars' (OQ-SN-4). *Integer conventions (QA-10; every boundary test needs the side of the equality).* On first bind `stage_dwell` is `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` (saturated), `harm_below_runs` and `pending` are 0, and `last_tell_epoch` is set to the live `tell_epoch`, so a stale BREACHED outcome at bind grants no startle; `last_onset_run` is -1 ("no onset yet", the gap gate passes) and `last_cid` is 0 (EXTERIOR, "none"), so the seat's first run in a real compartment opens its first visit *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING)*. D.2 reads `stage_dwell` as stored by the previous run and the counter is updated after it (+1, saturating, or 0 on a change), so the first legal change is the run after the counter reaches 25. All time windows (immunity `until_run`, `REPAIR_BIAS_S`, `HORROR_ENC_RESET_S`) are exclusive of their end run (immune while `run < until_run`; biased while `run - stamp < 300`); `LIE_GAP_S` is inclusive (a gap of 225 runs passes at exactly 225); distance tests (`HORROR_NEAR_R`, `HIDE_SAFE_R`, `CREW_R`) are inclusive (`d <= R` counts).
185	
186	**SN-4. Stages 0 to 3 with hysteresis and dwell.**
187	*Rule.* Stage is a pure function `stage_of(level, prev_stage, stage_dwell)` (D.2). Stage 0 sane; 1 the instruments; 2 the light; 3 the world's hue (ART 4.4) (registry: `sanity_stage`). Entry thresholds, strictly below: 1 at 70000, 2 at 55000, 3 at 25000 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (stage 2 raised from 45000 by the user ruling OQ-SN-38, derived in D.8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; exit thresholds, strictly above: entry plus `STAGE_HYST` 2000 (72000, 57000, 27000). A change is blocked until `stage_dwell` has reached `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` 25 (5 s). Harm eligibility and the victim tell are orthogonal flags (SN-11), never stages. **There is no stage 4.**
188	*Why.* The art bible has exactly three lie stages; PIPE:904 makes stage 3 the Filter's maximum; PIPE and PCI fixtures use 0 to 3. The SIM steps instantly; visual onset smoothing is the Filter's, subject to PR-13.
189	*Edge notes.* Conflict C1 routed to Failure & Trail: FT AC-88 "stages 0-4" must read "0-3". Two thresholds crossed in one run is impossible under the cap (36 mSU per run against gaps of at least 15000 between entry thresholds, after the OQ-SN-38 ruling; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: was 20000*) and arises only through a restore or debug force, where the stored stage is kept and a forced recompute moves directly to the target.

193	**SN-5. Exposure: a closed list of four true inputs.**
194	*Rule.* Exposure per run is `E = E1 + E2 + E3 + E4`. All are SIM values, true, read one way.
195	- **E1, depth and foreign body.** `RING_EXPOSURE[ring(p)]` (three depth rings 1 to 3, ring 1 the shallowest, Attention AT-6; `ring(p)` is `ring_of(actor_section(actor))`, and an unknown ring resolves to ring 1) plus `ABOARD_EXPOSURE` while the seat's body is not the home body (home-ness is `body_is_home`, orthogonal to ring, because the home ship moves). E1 is subject to the ambient floor (SN-29). Web Map & Transit publishes `ring(PlayerId)`, `body_is_home(PlayerId)` and `locus_kind(PlayerId)` as SIM reads and states the baseline, ring 1 for HOME, derelict A, derelict B and the pod (WM-27) *(Web Map & Transit, Designed; status refreshed 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **In the pod** (the seat's `loco_state` is IN_POD, or its body is the pod): `aboard` is false, so `ABOARD_EXPOSURE` is not charged; the ring is Attention's `held_ring` (WM-27), and `settled` is false. The hop is neither a refuge nor a drain beyond its ring term. This answers OQ-WM-6 (orchestrator ruling, logged). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

Status vocabulary: **designed** (GDD on disk, header "Designed"); **in flight** (GDD on disk as a draft, `Status: In Design`); **undesigned-provisional** (no file; this GDD is the first writer of its half). Type is the strength of the dependency for this system; "Counterpart row" says whether the neighbour's own GDD already lists Sanity (design-docs rule: dependencies must be bidirectional).

#### Sanity depends on (upstream)

| System | Type | Direction | Interface | Status | Counterpart row |

#### D.10 `horror_encounter_budget` *(E3; provisional on Horror)*

The `horror_encounter_budget` formula is defined as:

`pay_h = max(0, min(EXP_HORROR, HORROR_ENC_BUDGET - spent_h))` is horror `h`'s raw contribution to `E3` each run; `E3 = sum of pay_h over near h`; after the run's `net` is known, the **charge** is `delta = net(E3) - net(E3 = 0)` (both through the clamp of D.1; `delta >= 0`), spread over the near horrors in ascending ref order as `charge_h = min(pay_h, delta - sum of earlier charges)`, and `spent_h' = spent_h + charge_h` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: marginal charging, option (a) of OQ-SN-45; the budget was burned by contact the net cap absorbed)*; `spent_h' = 0` after `HORROR_ENC_RESET_S x 5` consecutive runs with `h` out of range; `min_encounters(a, b) = ceil((a - b) / HORROR_ENC_BUDGET)`

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EXP_HORROR` | int mSU/run | 20 (safe 0 to 28) | knob | rate while a registered HORROR is within `HORROR_NEAR_R` |
| `HORROR_ENC_BUDGET` | int mSU | 3000 (safe 1500 to 6000) | knob | most one horror can charge in one encounter |
| `HORROR_ENC_RESET_S` | int s | 120 (safe 30 to 300) | knob | out-of-range time that ends an encounter |
| `HORROR_NEAR_R` | int px | 288 (safe 144 to 480) | knob | distance from the seat's foot origin to the horror's `pos_px`; no light condition |
| `HORROR_TRACK_MAX` | int | 4 | knob | tracked refs; a fifth evicts the stalest encounter |
| `spent_h` | int mSU | 0 to `HORROR_ENC_BUDGET` | `sanity.ledger` `horror_enc[]` | spend in the current encounter |

**Output Range:** `pay_h` in 0 to 20; one horror charges at most 3000 mSU per encounter, reached after 150 runs = 30 s of contact when the net cap does not bind (when it binds, the charge is the marginal `delta`, so the encounter lasts longer and the budget is spent more slowly). **Farm bound** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED: restated from the lowest ambient floor, where routine play starts, and over 1 to `HORROR_TRACK_MAX` concurrent horrors; the earlier figure of about 25 encounters and over an hour was measured from stage-1 entry (55000 mSU) with one horror only and is superseded)*: from `min(AMBIENT_FLOOR)` 43000 to `SAN_HARM_ENTER` 15000 is 28000 mSU. With `k` horrors in contact at once the contact phase nets `k x 3000 - runs_contact x REC_IDLE` and each 120 s gap repays `REC_IDLE x 600` = 600, so the cycles needed are `ceil(28000 / (k x 3000 - contact_runs - 600))`: k = 1: contact 150 runs, `ceil(28000 / 2250)` = 13 encounters, 13 x 30 s + 12 x 120 s = 1830 s (30.5 min); k = 2: contact 163 runs (the cap binds, 6000 / 37 per run), `ceil(28000 / 5237)` = 6 cycles, about 796 s (13.3 min); k = 3: 244 runs, `ceil(28000 / 8156)` = 4 cycles, about 555 s (9.3 min); k = 4: 325 runs, `ceil(28000 / 11075)` = 3 cycles, about 435 s (7.3 min). The minimum over k is therefore about 435 s, still above the cap-only floor of D.4 (v) (185.6 s), so the budget does not weaken the lead invariant, and it is an **upper bound on speed** (marginal charging only slows it). Evict-and-retain (SN-30) means a fifth horror cannot refresh a spent budget, so these counts hold for any number of horrors in the world.
**Example:** a repelled horror held 250 px away: runs 1 to 150 pay 20 each (3000), run 151 onward pays `min(20, 0)` = 0; after the horror is out of range for 600 runs the budget resets to 3000 available.

(SN-2, SN-3, EC-SN-49, EC-SN-50) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED)*
1667:- **AC-SN-50 (auto)**: GIVEN built lie data WHEN inspected THEN every lie has a non-empty `leak_modes`, the first lie of a world has all three modes (gleam, the surface class's motion mode, sound) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, no lie at stage 2 or 3 has fewer than two, and every lie has `leak_modes & GLEAM != 0` and the motion bit set (only SOUND is ever dropped); GIVEN a subject with a PENDING or ACTIVE lie for a seat WHEN a new gated event on it arrives for that seat THEN no draw is made and no counter advances (one live lie per (seat, `subject_ref`), SN-16). (SN-15 L-L, SN-16)
1768:- **AC-SN-158 (auto, integration)**: GIVEN the real MVP slice fixture for fault 1 (the O2 pinhole at a clamp, LS-26), a seat in compartment Y one hop from the fault compartment X through an **open** opening, Y's `band_o2` OK, and a forced live COMFORT-direction lie (FALSE_OK, stage 1, the duct gauge in Y) WHEN the Graph runs the real fault timeline with no player action and the test records the Graph's measured times (`t_X_THIN`, and `t_Y_THIN` if reached) THEN (a) the lie stays ACTIVE at every run from its activation until the first run at which Y's band leaves OK or its life ends (L-G holds, no early INVALIDATION), and the test fails if the timeline takes Y out of OK within `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (the registered 10 s, the fairness gate's minimum warning, in place of the earlier bare "10 s") of activation, which would make the staging unplayable; (b) at every run while the lie is ACTIVE a **player-observable disagreement exists**: the fault's consequence-channel witness (HISS, `AIRFLOW`) is active, the opening's draught descriptor is active on Y's side, and the perception entry carries the gleam and the motion bit; (c) WHEN the seat then steps into X and X's band reaches THIN THEN the lie is INVALIDATED within one run of the seat's own band leaving OK, the glide-return begins, and the Suit's first body cue falls in the window before that Sanity run (`suit.vitals` runs at divisor 6, offset 2, and its STRAINED entry on band THIN is not rate-limited, so the cue may precede the INVALIDATE by 4 or 10 ticks: the Graph commits the band at T mod 6 = 2 and the Suit cues on that tick, and Sanity runs at T mod 12 = 0, 10 ticks later when T mod 12 = 2 and 4 ticks later when T mod 12 = 8; a comfort lie's ledger entry and a Suit cue are never both live beyond that window) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, and the test also records the **maximum seconds the displayed needle stays on the comfort side of the truth after the INVALIDATE** (the glide-return at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`, 32 to 38 s expected; reported as a measured value, with an ADVISORY ceiling of 40 s, and the finding that the gauge may still read comfort while the Suit says THIN is the accepted diegetic window of SN-15 L-G; it is a Filter-dependent measurement and waits for the Filter like AC-SN-166). The four timings are written to the test report as measured values (OQ-SN-18) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, RECOMMENDED)*. (SN-15 L-G, L-W, anchor beats 1 to 5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

prior_blockers_resolved: RESOLVED - repaired_recent[] vs G2 (AC-SN-133 L1705, AC-SN-150 L1629, plus L160, L301, L731/733, L980, L1676, L1843). AC-SN-133 now asserts that with the stub hp rise and the default REPAIR_BIAS_W 1 the field stays empty, the sanity.ledger key set is unchanged, there is no last-seen-hp key, and state_hash(PERSIST) equals the control session. Arithmetic re-checked: 2 x 300 = 600; at stage 3, 2 x 550 caps at 1000; in-window means run - S < 300.

RESOLVED - motion bit vs boot lint (L269, SN-23 schema L351, V-9/SNV-9 L1239, AC-SN-45 L1673, AC-SN-136 L1732). L269 now defines the motion bit by surface and adopts Perception Filter PF-15: NEEDLE drift plus wander; READOUT TICK or STALE plus the gleam breath; GLYPH and GLOW_SPRITE BREATH; MACHINE_SPRITE BREATH or rotor drift. SANITY_BOOT_LIE_TARGET_DATA refuses a row only when it can render no motion mode, and rows of surfaces 3, 4 and 5 are never refused. AC-SN-45 adds fixture rows that must pass boot. SNV-9 glyph uses BREATH and the schema leaves params {} empty. readout_mode is a pure function of kind (GLIDE 1 TICK; FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL 2 STALE) and costs no draw. findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-SN-25 against D.10 / D.1 (carried over from the previous review, G3/G4)
findings.finding: The previous review's AC-SN-25 finding did not land. L1627 still asserts that the level first falls below 15000 at '13 x 150 + 12 x 600 = 9150 runs' (k = 1) and 'about 2175' runs (k = 4), while also claiming the counts are asserted exactly. D.10 gives the budget-limited cycle (contact 150 / 163 / 244 / 325 runs, gap 600), so 9150 and 2175 are the ends of the final contact phase, not the first crossing. Worked check for k = 1: after 12 encounters the level is 43000 - 12 x 2250 = 16000, and 1001 mSU at net 19 per run needs 53 more runs, so the first crossing below 15000 is at run 9053. A correct implementation therefore fails this BLOCKING auto test. The 70000 case ('at least 25 encounters') also does not say that E1 is off.
findings.fix: Recompute every oracle from D.1/D.10 at registry defaults and restate it as 'first run at which level < 15000'. For k = 1 from 43000 that is run 9053, inside the 13th contact phase. Re-derive k = 2, 3 and 4 the same way (the previous review's simulation gave about 2816 and 2050 for k = 3 and 4). Alternatively, rename the oracle 'end of the Nth encounter' and drop the word 'first'. Add the E1 state to the 70000 case.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-SN-95 (stale after this pass)
findings.finding: L1749 still says each routed refresh 'C1 to C30' is recorded as owed and 'no neighbour file was edited by this stage'. The Cross-References table runs to C34. The 2026-10-28 cross-GDD pass (G6) did edit the siblings the GDD names (Perception Filter, Debug Overlay, kernel, Graph, Suit, Save/Load, registry). The AC cannot pass as written.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: 'GIVEN the Cross-References refresh table WHEN reviewed THEN every routed refresh C1 to C34 (and any C-id added later) is recorded either as closed (with the date and the edited sibling) or as owed to its owner; C8, C11, C16, C17, C18, C20, C31 and C34 are recorded closed'. Delete the 'no neighbour file was edited' clause.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-SN-151 against SN-23 / AC-SN-122 (carried over)
findings.finding: L1707 still asserts 'the same subject's inspect-card entry is present with the same start_run, end_run and leak_modes'. SN-23, C31 and AC-SN-122 (L1698) say the inspect card is not a separate perception entry, because the Filter draws it from the NEEDLE or READOUT entry. The AC asserts an entry the schema forbids and cannot pass.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: 'GIVEN a stage-1 GLIDE lie on a wall gauge WHEN sanity.perception is read THEN there is exactly one entry for the subject (NEEDLE or READOUT surface) and no entry with an inspect-card surface; the card's lie is asserted by AC-PF-xx (Filter) from that entry'. Inspecting must never show the truth, which is a Filter-side test and should move there.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-SN-123 against SN-16 gate order (carried over)
findings.finding: L1699 expects 'no event at r+99, event at r+100'. SN-16 (L293) evaluates the debounce at processing time, and events inside the 10-run batch window are held until the window closes. The stamp is therefore written at about r+10, not at r. The oracle is wrong for a lit-on-entry subject, and 'no event' conflicts with 'one event per (seat, subject, visit)', since evented[] is emptied on the compartment change and the event is formed and then gated.
findings.fix: State the oracle on the processing run: 'the first event is processed at run P (stamp P); a re-entry whose event is processed at P+99 is refused by the debounce with no draw and no counter advance; one processed at P+100 passes it'. Give the batch-close offset explicitly, so that formation run = processing run - (batch_end_run - formation run).

findings.section: Detailed Rules: SN-16 batch window / visit rule (carried over)
findings.finding: The spec still does not say what happens to events held in the ENTRY_BATCH_RUNS window when the seat leaves the compartment (cid(P) != last_cid) before batch_end_run. Walking through a compartment in under 2 s is ordinary play. evented[], debounce[], visit counters, last_onset_run and state_hash depend on the answer, so two faithful implementations can diverge.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to SN-16 and one Edge Case plus an AC. Suggested rule: held events are discarded on a compartment change. evented[] is emptied with them, no debounce stamp is written, no draw is made, and batch_end_run clears with entry_pending. AC: enter B, leave at window run 4, assert zero draws and an unchanged ledger shape.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs / D.8 / AC-SN-171: ABOARD_EXPOSURE safe range and the STAGE2_UNREACHABLE reason (carried over)
findings.finding: D.8 constraint 1 (L848) says that at the 14-minute visit the stage-2 reachability relation needs ABOARD_EXPOSURE >= 12 in ring 1, and that 8 fails (net 7 needs 21.4 min). Tuning L613 and L1113, and the registry ABOARD_EXPOSURE row, still publish 'safe 8 to 20'. The user-ruled stage-2 reach is therefore broken by values the GDD calls safe. AC-SN-171 fails with the named reason STAGE2_UNREACHABLE, which is not in the closed SANITY_BOOT_* set (L174) and is not defined as a test-only reason.
findings.fix: Change the safe range to 12 to 20 in the SN-5 table, Tuning and the registry. Explain the low end by the D.8 relation with L_ref_runs 4200 (net >= 11). Either add STAGE2_UNREACHABLE to SANITY_BOOT_REASONS (and the registry) or say it is the test failure label and not a boot reason. Recheck the 'stage 1 only after 14.3 min aboard at 8' cell.

findings.section: Detailed Rules L-2I / Interactions (Suit row) / Cross-References C32 / OQ-SN-46 (carried over, G1)
findings.finding: Sanity still reads two invented Suit names, carry_state(player_id) and scanner_equippable(player_id). A grep of suit-and-equipment.md finds zero hits. Suit publishes carried_instance and tool_in_hand (SE lines 483, 1469, 1613) and its equip_tool BUSY rule (SE-11). Under G1 the consumer conforms to the publisher. With the fail-safe stub, every seat reads as carrying and not scanner-equippable. That silently removes the single-instrument-loop comfort-lie supply, so the MVP anchor staging depends on a read that does not exist.
findings.fix: Rename the reads in SN-15 L-2I, the Interactions table, C32 and OQ-SN-46 to the published names. carrying = (carried_instance != 0). scanner_equippable = (carried_instance == 0 and tool_scanner is held in a tool slot, via tool_in_hand / the slot view). Drop 'provisional contract' for these two and keep the stub only for a missing view. Add one AC that the stub path is not taken in the MVP slice.

findings.section: Registry design/registry/entities.yaml: SAN_HARM_EXIT (carried over)
findings.finding: The registry unit text still says 'range 15360 (D.9 boot assertion) to 25000'. The GDD (Formulas L683, L864, Tuning L1092) says the D.9 minimum is 15612 (SAN_HARM_ENTER + 17 x 36). A retune to 15400 passes the registry range and fails the D.9 boot assertion. The sanity.perception entry_fields row also ends with a repaired_r... clause that should be re-read against G2.
findings.fix: Update the SAN_HARM_EXIT range to 15612 to 25000 (revised 2026-10-28). Re-read the sanity.perception entry_fields tail so that it says repaired_recent[] is a reserved, always-empty ledger field and not a perception field.

findings.section: Detailed Rules: lie_targets.json row schema (L269, SN-23, AC-SN-45)
findings.finding: Gate (a) of SN-23 now reads the subject row's authored OK and alarm intervals to compute c_dial. The row schema in L269, in the 'Data' part of SN-23 and in AC-SN-45 lists only surface, needle_len_px and the readout modes. Sanity's own data contract therefore omits a field it reads. The field is carried as a provisional contract (OQ-SN-46 and R9).
findings.fix: Add 'ok_interval_pm and alarm_interval_pm per NEEDLE row (Instruments' calibration record)' to the L269 row list, and a boot check that c_dial is non-zero. Alternatively state that Sanity reads c_dial from the calibration record through the Filter's D.3 helper.

findings.section: Player Fantasy L60 / Overview L70 (stale wording after the offset change)
findings.finding: Both say the Suit's first cue 'arrives within the same 12-tick Sanity run as the lie's end'. After the Graph/Suit stagger, the Suit cues at T mod 6 = 2 and Sanity ends the lie 4 or 10 ticks later, so the cue comes before the ledger end. AC-SN-158(c) states this correctly. The fantasy text still reads as simultaneous.
findings.fix: Reword to 'the Suit's cue falls 4 to 10 ticks (0.07 to 0.17 s) before the run that ends the lie, and the lie never outlives the cue by a run'. The anchor beat is unchanged.

findings.section: Header / document hygiene
findings.finding: 'Last Verified' is 2026-10-27 while 'Last Updated' is 2026-10-28. The CD-GDD-ALIGN approval note still says it predates the amendments and 'is to be re-run before sprint planning'. The file is 550 KB, with normative rules interleaved with multi-KB '(Amended ...)' history. The leftovers found in this review (AC-SN-95, AC-SN-151) trace to that reading cost.
findings.fix: Re-run CD-GDD-ALIGN after the sibling pass settles. Move the amendment history into the review log or a Revision-history appendix, leaving one current statement per rule, as the previous review recommended.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-SN-25 against D.10 / D.1 (carried over from the previous review, G3/G4)
findings.finding: The previous review's AC-SN-25 finding did not land. L1627 still asserts that the level first falls below 15000 at '13 x 150 + 12 x 600 = 9150 runs' (k = 1) and 'about 2175' runs (k = 4), while also claiming the counts are asserted exactly. D.10 gives the budget-limited cycle (contact 150 / 163 / 244 / 325 runs, gap 600), so 9150 and 2175 are the ends of the final contact phase, not the first crossing. Worked check for k = 1: after 12 encounters the level is 43000 - 12 x 2250 = 16000, and 1001 mSU at net 19 per run needs 53 more runs, so the first crossing below 15000 is at run 9053. A correct implementation therefore fails this BLOCKING auto test. The 70000 case ('at least 25 encounters') also does not say that E1 is off.
findings.fix: Recompute every oracle from D.1/D.10 at registry defaults and restate it as 'first run at which level < 15000'. For k = 1 from 43000 that is run 9053, inside the 13th contact phase. Re-derive k = 2, 3 and 4 the same way (the previous review's simulation gave about 2816 and 2050 for k = 3 and 4). Alternatively, rename the oracle 'end of the Nth encounter' and drop the word 'first'. Add the E1 state to the 70000 case.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-SN-95 (stale after this pass)
findings.finding: L1749 still says each routed refresh 'C1 to C30' is recorded as owed and 'no neighbour file was edited by this stage'. The Cross-References table runs to C34. findings.fix: Rewrite as: 'GIVEN the Cross-References refresh table WHEN reviewed THEN every routed refresh C1 to C34 (and any C-id added later) is recorded either as closed (with the date and the edited sibling) or as owed to its owner; C8, C11, C16, C17, C18, C20, C31 and C34 are recorded closed'. Delete the 'no neighbour file was edited' clause.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-SN-151 against SN-23 / AC-SN-122 (carried over)
findings.finding: L1707 still asserts 'the same subject's inspect-card entry is present with the same start_run, end_run and leak_modes'. SN-23, C31 and AC-SN-122 (L1698) say the inspect card is not a separate perception entry, because the Filter draws it from the NEEDLE or READOUT entry. The AC asserts an entry the schema forbids and cannot pass.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: 'GIVEN a stage-1 GLIDE lie on a wall gauge WHEN sanity.perception is read THEN there is exactly one entry for the subject (NEEDLE or READOUT surface) and no entry with an inspect-card surface; the card's lie is asserted by AC-PF-xx (Filter) from that entry'. Inspecting must never show the truth, which is a Filter-side test and should move there.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-SN-123 against SN-16 gate order (carried over)
findings.finding: L1699 expects 'no event at r+99, event at r+100'. SN-16 (L293) evaluates the debounce at processing time, and events inside the 10-run batch window are held until the window closes. The stamp is therefore written at about r+10, not at r. The oracle is wrong for a lit-on-entry subject, and 'no event' conflicts with 'one event per (seat, subject, visit)', since evented[] is emptied on the compartment change and the event is formed and then gated.
findings.fix: State the oracle on the processing run: 'the first event is processed at run P (stamp P); a re-entry whose event is processed at P+99 is refused by the debounce with no draw and no counter advance; one processed at P+100 passes it'. Give the batch-close offset explicitly, so that formation run = processing run - (batch_end_run - formation run).

findings.section: Detailed Rules: SN-16 batch window / visit rule (carried over)
findings.finding: The spec still does not say what happens to events held in the ENTRY_BATCH_RUNS window when the seat leaves the compartment (cid(P) != last_cid) before batch_end_run. Walking through a compartment in under 2 s is ordinary play. evented[], debounce[], visit counters, last_onset_run and state_hash depend on the answer, so two faithful implementations can diverge.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to SN-16 and one Edge Case plus an AC. Suggested rule: held events are discarded on a compartment change. evented[] is emptied with them, no debounce stamp is written, no draw is made, and batch_end_run clears with entry_pending. AC: enter B, leave at window run 4, assert zero draws and an unchanged ledger shape.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs / D.8 / AC-SN-171: ABOARD_EXPOSURE safe range and the STAGE2_UNREACHABLE reason (carried over)

Either add STAGE2_UNREACHABLE to SANITY_BOOT_REASONS (and the registry) or say it is the test failure label and not a boot reason. Recheck the 'stage 1 only after 14.3 min aboard at 8' cell.

findings.section: Detailed Rules L-2I / Interactions (Suit row) / Cross-References C32 / OQ-SN-46 (carried over, G1)

findings.fix: Rename the reads in SN-15 L-2I, the Interactions table, C32 and OQ-SN-46 to the published names. carrying = (carried_instance != 0). scanner_equippable = (carried_instance == 0 and tool_scanner is held in a tool slot, via tool_in_hand / the slot view). findings.section: Registry design/registry/entities.yaml: SAN_HARM_EXIT (carried over)

findings.section: Detailed Rules: lie_targets.json row schema (L269, SN-23, AC-SN-45)
